title: 1/5 StarsTransparency" is just a buzzword for gatekeeping.
content: 1/5 Stars - "Transparency" is just a buzzword for gatekeeping.  Spotify likes to talk about "royalty transparency," but their actions tell a different story. They’ve turned the music economy into a "pay-to-play" system that actively punishes small, independent artists.  The 1,000-stream minimum threshold is a total joke. It essentially means that if you are a rising artist or a niche creator, your work is worth $0.00 until you hit their arbitrary metric. To make it worse, they only pay for the streams after that threshold, effectively pocketing the revenue from millions of smaller tracks that make up the backbone of their library.  Don't let the corporate emails fool you—this isn't about being "responsible" or helping you understand your "revenue opportunity." It’s about cutting off the little guy to pad the bottom line. If you care about supporting independent music, look elsewhere.

title: Spotify is just a money grabbing app
content: Spotify is an absolute masterclass in how to take a brilliant idea—instant access to millions of songs—and completely suffocate it under layers of incompetence, greed, and baffling design decisions.  Let’s start with the free version, which isn’t so much a service as it is an endurance test. The ads aren’t just frequent—they’re relentless, repetitive, and somehow engineered to be as irritating as possible. It’s less “listen to music” and more “occasionally hear a song between audio torture sessions.” Whoever decided the ads should be louder than the music deserves a special place in UX hell.  Then you upgrade, thinking you’re escaping the nightmare. You’re not. You’ve just paid to be mildly less annoyed. The so-called “premium” experience still manages to feel half-baked. Features break, downloads vanish, and the app behaves like it’s being held together by duct tape and wishful thinking.  The interface? A chaotic, over-engineered disaster. It constantly rearranges itself like it’s ashamed of its own layout. Want to find a song you liked yesterday? Good luck. Spotify would rather shove 15 “curated” playlists down your throat than let you access your own music without a scavenger hunt. It’s like the app resents the idea that you might know what you want to listen to.  And the recommendations—wow. Spotify loves to brag about its algorithm, but it seems to have the memory of a goldfish with a head injury. It cycles the same songs endlessly, pretending it’s “discovering” things for you when it’s really just stuck on repeat. It’s less personalized and more aggressively clueless.  Performance-wise, it’s a mess. Random pauses, songs skipping, the app freezing at the worst possible moments—it’s like every update is a gamble to see what new problem they can introduce. Offline mode is especially laughable, as if the app forgets its entire purpose the second your signal drops.  At this point, Spotify doesn’t feel like a music platform—it feels like a bloated, self-important middleman that actively makes music harder to enjoy. It’s impressive, in the worst possible way, how consistently it manages to get in its own way.  If there were an award for turning something simple into something unbearable, Spotify wouldn’t just win—it would curate a playlist about it and still somehow mess that up.

Incompetence & Delays: After two hours of back-and-forth, the third agent (Vijaya) joined and immediately went silent for 20 minutes. title: Incompetent
content: I must confess, I’ve encountered few services as utterly incompetent as Spotify’s approach to customer care. I changed countries — a simple, everyday reality for a frequent traveler — and now find myself trapped in an absurdly Kafkaesque loop.  Their solution? Obtain a local credit card. Yes, you read that correctly. Because apparently, if my profile reflects my current country of residence, and my card is issued elsewhere, the very notion of logic is discarded. One wonders: am I now required to maintain a fleet of local credit cards around the globe just to pay for what should be a seamless digital service?  Spotify, let me be crystal clear. The issue is not my card. It is your inability to reconcile a user’s profile with a reality that exists outside your narrow, myopic system. I expected elegance, efficiency, discretion — what I received was amateurism, frustration, and the maddening sensation that I am negotiating with a particularly dim-witted bureaucracy.  If you value your time, your patience, or your dignity, tread carefully. Spotify’s customer service is not merely lacking; it is an affront to reason itself.

title: Spotify feels like it slowly turns on…
content: Spotify feels like it slowly turns on you once you’re locked in. You pay every month and still feel squeezed. Prices go up, features shuffle around, and things that used to be simple now feel gated. You open the app and it’s playlists being pushed, podcasts you didn’t ask for, promos everywhere. It stops feeling like your music and starts feeling like their funnel. Recommendations get lazy. You listen to one thing and they beat it to death for weeks. Try to discover something new and it circles back to the same safe stuff. You end up skipping more than listening. Offline bugs, random glitches, downloads disappearing for no reason. Stuff you expect to just work suddenly doesn’t. Then there’s the whole control thing. Artists you follow get buried, releases don’t show up, and the app decides what you should hear instead. You’re paying but still fighting the product. It feels bloated, pushy, and way too comfortable taking your money while slowly making the experience worse.

title: Should be called Greedify
content: I’ve been a loyal Spotify Premium subscriber since around 2019, and over the years I’ve spent close to $900 on this platform. Until now, I’ve genuinely enjoyed using it — but this recent decision to raise the subscription price to $16 a month is honestly infuriating and disappointing.  There have been no meaningful improvements or new features to justify this increase. Spotify keeps mentioning “innovation” and “investment in customer experience,” but as someone who’s been paying for six years, I’ve seen no real evidence of that. The app functions pretty much the same — ad-free music and playlists. If ad-free listening is still the only real benefit, then charging $16 a month feels like pure greed, not innovation.  Spotify claims to offer “plans tailored to different needs,” but these mainly benefit students, couples, and families. What about single users, retirees, or low-income individuals who don’t qualify for those discounts? The lack of fair or flexible options for these groups feels exclusionary, especially at a time when the cost of living is rising globally.  What frustrates me most is the templated responses from customer support. I understand they have to follow protocol, but nothing in their message addressed the real question — what exactly are we paying more for? If there’s no visible improvement, it’s impossible to justify a higher price tag.  I’ve supported Spotify for years because I believed in the service, but this latest move shows a lack of respect for long-term subscribers. It’s disappointing to see a company so focused on profit over people. I will no longer be paying for this service!  Shame on Spotify for forgetting the loyalty of its users.

title: Losing a premium user due to how you treat your free users.
content: Having been a Spotify Premium user for 3-4 years now, I am unable to renew my subscription due to current financial constraints. I figured I'd use the free--with ads-- version for a while until I can renew. That said, I am so disappointed by the amount of ads you are forced to listen to that it's not even worth it. There's a good chance I won't renew with Spotify because I'm ready to find a new service after only five days of free listening.  To show what I'm talking about, here is an hour worth of listening and how many ads I had to endure in that time. If you consider that the total amount of ads was 9 minutes out of 65 minutes, that means that ~15% of what you listen to is ads. While that isn't a disproportionately large amount (compared to old-school TV stations which were often 25% ads), the problem is it is impossible to get into your music when you are interrupted every couple songs by loud ads. Some of the ad sets were no more than 6.5 minutes apart. As a result you only get to hear 2-3 songs between 1.5 minute ad sets. This is particularly unbearable for someone like me who likes to listen to music at high volume, just to be blasted with obnoxiously loud ads after every 2nd or 3rd song.  12:03 - 4 ads 1.5m (ended at 12:04.5) 12:12.5 - 3 ads 1.5m (ended at 12:14) 12:20.5 - 2 ads 1.5m (ended at 12:22) -- One song automatically skipped after 30 seconds and next ads came even sooner at 6.5 minutes 12:29.5 - 3 ads 1.5m (ended at 12:31) 12:39.75 - 3 ads 1.5m (ended at 12.41.25) -- Long 5s+ pause between multiple songs for no reason on this set 12:53.75 - 3 ads 1.75m (ended at 12:55.5) 01:07.5 - 3 ads 1.25m (ended at 01:08.75)  This is abrasive and abusive towards your free users. You could easily do longer ad sets with longer ad-free listening in between so that people can actually turn up their favorite music and enjoy it without being jolted with anxiety every 7.5 minutes when an obnoxious ad blasts over the speakers.  Furthermore, I noticed a couple other things that have degraded my opinion of Spotify.  1) A song automatically skipped a few seconds inn. While this happens occasionally even with Premium, this time I was made to listen to ads even sooner, after a mere 6.5 minutes, despite that I'm not the one who skipped the song. 2) During one set there were multiple long pauses between songs for no reason. I have 300MB download speed, and this never happened with Premium, so I know it wasn't on my end. This leads me to believe that these random 5 second pauses are just to pad your listening and decrease costs while keeping the same amount of ad revenue between songs sets. 3) When my premium first expired I was getting 10-20 minutes between ad sets. The longer I have listened without premium, the less actual music I get to listen to. In only five days, 10-20 minutes has degraded to less than 9 on average. title: Spotify Using Facial Recognition? As a Cybersecurity Professional, This is Reckless.
content: Facial recognition for a music app is not just unnecessary — it’s a security risk.  As someone in cybersecurity, I can tell you: biometric data is not like a password. You can’t change your face when it gets breached. Storing or even processing facial data creates a massive attack surface for hackers and data brokers — and Spotify doesn’t have a clean enough record to justify this level of invasive tech.  This isn’t banking or healthcare. It’s music. There is no reason for a streaming service to request biometric scans. Once this data exists, it’s a target — and the user has zero control over how it’s stored, shared, or potentially sold.  Facial recognition is already notorious for bias, misidentification, and abuse. For Spotify to normalize this in the entertainment space is a terrifying precedent.  If this isn’t immediately walked back, I’ll be canceling my subscription and advising everyone — clients, friends, and colleagues — to do the same. Your playlist is not worth your privacy.

I reached out and spoke to two agents — Paula and Pandita. They were kind in tone, full of empathy, but unfortunately, empathy was all they could offer. Both said their “hands were tied” and that guidelines don’t allow refunds beyond a certain window — even when the subscription was barely used and I was clearly in distress.  Spotify may be following policy, but where’s the human side of customer care? One payment might mean nothing to a corporation, but it meant food or fuel to me.  If they truly listened — as they said they did — this wouldn’t have ended in a scripted shutdown. It would’ve ended with compassion.  Deeply disappointed. If you’re considering a trial and you live on a tight budget — beware.

title: Ripping off UK users
content: I’m a long-time Spotify user in the UK, and I’m writing to express my concern about your current pricing structure.  The monthly Premium cost in the UK (£10.99) is significantly higher than in many other countries — including the US, Sweden, and Hungary — even though those countries often have higher average incomes and VAT rates.  For example: • In Sweden, Premium is around £9.00/month • In Hungary, it’s around £4.40/month • Even in the US, after tax, it’s still cheaper than the UK  This pricing disparity feels increasingly unfair, especially since the service provided is identical worldwide. It creates the impression that UK customers are being overcharged simply because we’re seen as a “Tier 1” market.  I urge you to review your regional pricing and consider making it more equitable. Otherwise, I — and many others — will seriously reconsider continuing our subscriptions when other services offer better value.

title: Extremely Poor Refund Process and Communication
content: I am writing to express my extreme dissatisfaction with Spotify's handling of a refund. On February 11, 2025, Spotify agreed to refund me approximately £200 due to an issue where they incorrectly charged me for several months after I cancelled a service. It is now May 20th, and I am STILL waiting for this refund.  I was initially told the refund would take "weeks." After several weeks passed, I contacted Spotify on April 12, 2025, and was informed that the refund was in its "final stages of processing." Since then, I have made multiple attempts to get a clear answer from Spotify about when I can expect to receive my money. The responses I have received have been consistently vague, unhelpful, and often ignored.  This delay of over 3 months is unacceptable. Spotify has failed to meet its obligations under the Consumer Rights Act 2015, which requires refunds to be issued without undue delay. Their poor communication and lack of action have caused me significant inconvenience and frustration.  I strongly advise caution when dealing with Spotify, particularly regarding refunds. Their customer service is inadequate, and they seem to have no regard for their customers' time or legal rights. I am now being forced to pursue other avenues to recover my money.

title: How Spotify Destroys Family Values

But apparently, Spotify thinks it means “everyone crammed under one roof.” Sorry, grandma down the road or college kid across the state – you’re out of the club.  It’s like they’re running a stealth campaign against actual families. “Oh, you love your cousin who lives five minutes away? Not family enough!” Spotify wants your ‘family’ to come with GPS coordinates, which kinda feels like a reality show gone wrong: “Who Survives The Address Check?”  Between cracking playlists and cracking the meaning of family, Spotify might just need to rename its plan the “Cohabitant Plan” and own it. Because hey, as soon as you step outside the front door, you’re basically disowned from that sweet, sweet ‘family’ discount.  In short: If you enjoy living at a different address than your folks – or, you know, real life – Spotify’s got a brand-new definition of “family values” for you. Good luck.

title: Unethical, Predatory, and Completely Disappointing Experience
content: I have never encountered a more underhanded and deceptive service than Spotify. Their so-called "free trial" is nothing more than a thinly veiled trap designed to ensnare unsuspecting users and bleed them dry. Despite never actually using their Premium features, I found myself charged for a service I neither wanted nor benefited from, and all without so much as a courtesy reminder.  Their support team is utterly useless, parading empty apologies and rigidly quoting irrelevant policies instead of taking any genuine steps toward a fair resolution. It’s painfully obvious they’re trained to stonewall customers with a smug sense of self-righteousness, refusing refunds in cases that are clearly unfair. They hide behind their “14-day” nonsense and never make any attempt at basic consumer-friendly notifications before slapping charges onto your account.  Unlike reputable companies that show basic human decency—sending out timely reminders or easily accommodating honest mistakes—Spotify relies on customers’ oversight to make money off them. They are the definition of a shameless, morally bankrupt enterprise that treats people as dollar signs rather than valued patrons.  Avoid Spotify at all costs. Their business model is tantamount to a scam—sign you up under the guise of a free trial, fail to remind you of renewal, and then arrogantly refuse any refunds once they quietly drain your money. There are plenty of honest, transparent music services out there. Spotify is not one of them.

title: Quite good, but a lot of issues need fixing still
content: I feel like we’re giving Spotify a hard time on here for things that aren’t entirely fair, or at least not that relevant.  The main argument for Spotify, which is what puts it over it’s competitors like Tidal, Apple Music and Deezer, is simply it’s algorithm. If there is one thing they do well, it is putting people onto good music, and in my opinion, that is one of the main tasks a service like Spotify needs to accomplish.  That being said, there are a few very good reasons, especially with recent adjustments, that bitter the taste a bit. One thing, that I as a musician myself have to point out immediately, is the fact that they pay the artists very poorly. About half of what Apple Music pays per stream.  I also feel like it should be quite possible for Spotify to compete with the likes of Tidal in high quality audio, which is one of Tidal’s key advantages.  Political correctness, in censoring Rechts-Rock, could also be taken a bit more seriously, as Deezer is showing off.  The new day-lists are a very good addition in my opinion, however I would prefer if the algorithm would still favor music of artists I already enjoy and listen to regularly on the main page, rather than highest selling releases, regardless of genre and likeness to my taste.  Also, please make the new music tab more quickly accessible again. You had that down previously, why did you change it?  All in all, I’m sitting somewhere around a 3,5. As of now, I’m willing to lean towards 4, but I’m unsure how long these factors can be left untreated until that changes. One competitor adjusting it’s algorithm, could be all it takes before people really start leaving, and it feels like they aren’t aware enough of that.

title: Disappointed with Recent Price Increase

Competitors like Qobuz offer CD-quality music at a lower price, making the decision to stay with Spotify more difficult.  Furthermore, Spotify's failure to upgrade its audio quality to formats like WAV/CD lossless is frustrating, especially in today's audio landscape where high-fidelity options are readily available.  Unless Spotify addresses these concerns promptly, I'll be forced to cancel my subscription and explore alternatives. It's time for Spotify to prioritize customer satisfaction and justify its pricing decisions.

title: I've been using Spotify in UA
content: I've been using Spotify for a while now, and it's hard to imagine my daily routine without it. As a music streaming platform, Spotify stands out with its vast library of songs, covering almost every genre imaginable. Whether I'm in the mood for the latest hits, classic rock, or even obscure indie tracks, Spotify seems to have it all.  The user interface is one of the highlights for me. It's clean, intuitive, and makes navigating through the extensive music collection a breeze. Creating playlists is super easy and fun, and the way Spotify suggests new music based on my listening habits is impressively accurate.  Another feature I absolutely love is the ability to download songs and listen offline. It's a lifesaver for my commutes and travels. The sound quality is consistently good, and I haven't experienced any significant issues with streaming.  Spotify's social features add an extra layer of enjoyment. Sharing playlists with friends or seeing what others are listening to is a great way to discover new music and stay connected.  Their subscription model is fair, in my opinion. The free version offers a lot, but I opted for the premium subscription to avoid ads and get better sound quality. To me, the cost is justified by the value I get out of it.  In summary, Spotify has been a fantastic service for all my music needs. It's user-friendly, offers a great selection of music, and the personalized experience makes it feel like my own personal DJ. Highly recommended for any music lover!

Its vast library of over millions of songs across various genres, languages, and cultures caters to the diverse musical tastes of its users worldwide. The platform's commitment to supporting artists through initiatives like 'Spotify for Artists' and features like 'Canvas' (which allows artists to personalize their tracks with looping visuals) demonstrates its dedication to promoting and empowering musicians.  Furthermore, Spotify's podcasts and audio content add depth to its offerings, featuring a wide range of topics, from educational series to entertaining discussions, making it a one-stop destination for both music and spoken-word content.  In conclusion, Spotify sets the gold standard for music streaming services, combining an extensive music library, intuitive interface, personalized recommendations, and support for artists. title: Spotify has gone downhill, very weird activities recently
content: Spotify has gone downhill, very weird activities recently. I've been a musician on Spotify for several years, but recently something has changed there, not for the better. I received email stating that "one or more of your playlists will no longer be publicly available" . . . with absolutely no explanation, except to include a URL to a very long and complex "terms and conditions" site. Any attempt to reach anyone at Spotify about this is impossible. Their support phn #s no longer exist, there is no direct email adr except to their generic "office", which never responds. There is a live chat, human agents can eventually be reached, but the minute I mention this particular issue, they IMMEDIATELY END THE CHAT SESSION. I've tried 5 times to ask, very politely, to at least have some sort of explanation, only to be told to "refer to the email", which is a "do not reply" email, with no usable contact references, and then the chat session is immediately terminated, without warning . . . this is really weird. What's going on with Spotify???  All of my material is synth instrumental, no lyrics, or anything else that could possibly be "offensive" to anyone. And yet, there is no way to even find out what may have caused this weird playlist restriction. Also, I've had several seemingly random password episodes, all within the past few weeks, where Spotify suddenly forces me to change my password (again, with no explanation at all). I don't have any mobile devices at all, but keeps insisting I have to sync all of my devices with a Spotify app (I do all my work on their website, from PC desktop, there are no "devices" nor do I use their "app".) If Spotify is under some sort of new management, or cost saving full automation for their processes, it's not working, am already looking for new alternatives.  Apparently a growing number of other Spotify users have been having the same issues. Is anyone there actually seeing these reviews?
